OpenCode Prompt: MoshineSites Portfolio
Context: Generate 4 complete site templates in separate subfolders. Frontend-only: Next.js static export. Backend-hosted: Next.js full-stack with API routes + database.

2 Frontend: Restaurant, SaaS Dashboard | 2 Backend: Booking System, Analytics Dashboard

Design System (Consistent)
Colors:
  --bg-primary: #ffffff
  --bg-secondary: #f4efe8
  --text-primary: #1a1a1a
  --text-secondary: #6b6b6b
  --brand: #5a4a42
  --border: #e0ddd8
  --error: #c94a4a

Spacing (8px base):
  xs=4px, sm=8px, md=16px, lg=24px, xl=32px, 2xl=48px, 3xl=64px

Responsive:
  Mobile: 0-640px (1 col, hamburger)
  Tablet: 640-1024px (2 col)
  Desktop: 1024px+ (3 col)
Frontend-Only (Static Export)
1. Restaurant Site
Tech: Next.js 14, React, Tailwind CSS, static export

Content: Logo (Ember & Wood), sticky nav, hero, about (2-col), featured dishes (3-col grid), gallery, testimonials, hours/contact, reservation CTA, footer.

UX: Smooth scroll, image lazy loading, hover animations, lightbox gallery, no API calls.

2. SaaS Dashboard Landing
Tech: Next.js 14, React, Framer Motion, static export

Concept: TaskFlow — task management app

Content: Hero, features (3-col grid), interactive demo (live task widget), pricing (3 tiers), testimonials, CTA footer.

Key: Fully interactive task widget (add, complete, delete). React useState. Framer Motion animations. No backend.

Backend-Hosted (Full-Stack)
3. Restaurant Booking System
Tech: Next.js 14 full-stack, React, SQLite

Public: Hero, about, booking widget (date, time, party size, guest info), testimonials, contact.

Admin: /admin route. Login (hardcoded password or env). Table of all bookings. Actions: confirm, mark done, delete.

API: /api/bookings (GET, POST, DELETE, PATCH). SQLite bookings table. Validation: no past dates, no overlaps.

Database: SQLite file-based (booking.db). Seed with sample bookings. Include .env.example and README.

4. Analytics Dashboard
Tech: Next.js 14 full-stack, React, SQLite or Supabase

Concept: Metrics — content analytics (like TweetDeck)

Dashboard: 3 metric cards (views, engagement, active). Feed of content items (updates every 5s). Right sidebar: trending topics. Click item → detail page with chart.

Routes: /dashboard (main), /settings (theme toggle, polling freq), /analytics (7-day overview).

API: /api/metrics, /api/feed, /api/content/[id]. Real-time: backend updates views/engagement every 5s.

Chart: Recharts line chart (7-day performance). Seed with 15-20 sample content items.

Requirements
Consistent design system across all 4 (colors, spacing, typography)
Responsive: mobile 640px, tablet 1024px, desktop
Semantic HTML, accessible (WCAG AA, 4.5:1 contrast, 44px touch targets)
Smooth, intentional interactions (no janky animations, respect prefers-reduced-motion)
Fast (minimal deps, lazy-loaded images, optimized CSS)
Production-deployable (no console errors, no broken links)
Clean, readable React components (functional, hooks)
Tailwind CSS only (no external UI libraries)
Frontend Output
Run: npm run build → outputs static files, ready to deploy to Vercel/Netlify/GitHub Pages

Backend Output
Run: npm install → set .env → npm run dev → fully functional with real data, API routes working, database populated

Include: .env.example, README.md with setup steps, seed script

Success: All 4 sites look polished, feel fast, and are portfolio-grade. You'll review, test, and show screenshots for refinement.

The user wants me to generate 4 complete site templates in separate subfolders in the `/home/daniel/template-sites` directory: 1. Restaurant Site (frontend-only, static export) 2. SaaS Dashboard Landing (frontend-only, static export) 3. Restaurant Booking System (backend, full-stack with SQLite) 4. Analytics Dashboard (backend, full-stack with SQLite) This is a large multi-step task. Let me follow the orchestrator workflow: Phase 1: Intake - check the working directory Phase 2: Planning - create PLAN.md Phase 3: Execution - delegate to agents Phase 4: Verification Let me start by checking the current state of the working directory, then create a plan. Given the scale of this task (4 complete Next.js sites), I should: 1. First look at the working directory 2. Create a plan 3. Delegate implementation to agents (per orchestrator principles, delegate don't do) However, I also need to be pragmatic. The Task tool with subagents can be used for parallel work. Each site is independent, so I can delegate each site's build to a separate agent (or do it myself with careful implementation). The instructions say "Delegate to agents - NOT do work yourself" but also the task is very concrete and detailed. Let me think about the best approach. Creating 4 complete Next.js sites is a huge amount of work. Each site needs: - package.json - next.config - tailwind config - app router pages - components - etc. For the backend sites: - SQLite database setup - API routes - Seed scripts - README, .env.example Given the constraints, I'll delegate each site to a `general` agent or `architect`... Actually for building, the `general` agent is the best fit since it can execute multi-step tasks. The `tdd-guide` for test-first... but the user didn't emphasize tests here, though the orchestrator mandates TDD. For template sites, tests are less critical but the instructions say TDD mandatory. I'll have agents write core logic tests where reasonable but focus on the deliverable. Actually, let me reconsider. Since this is a very concrete, well-specified task, and my tools are directly available, I could do the work myself in the main thread. But the orchestrator instructions strongly say "Delegate to agents". Let me use the Task tool with `general` agents for each site, running them in parallel where possible. However, there's a practical concern: agents running in parallel creating Next.js projects with npm install might conflict or take long. Each agent works in its own subfolder though, so that's fine. But npm installs take time. Alternatively, I can scaffold the projects myself quickly and then... no, let me just delegate. Actually, let me be efficient. I'll: 1. Check the directory state 2. Create PLAN.md 3. Create the base design system to share across sites (maybe not needed since each Next.js project needs its own tailwind config anyway) 4. Delegate each site to a `general` agent with detailed specs 5. Run builds to verify 6. Fix issues Wait, but can I run agents in parallel? Yes - "Launch multiple agents concurrently whenever possible, to maximize performance; to do that, use a single message with multiple tool uses". But each agent doing `npm install` etc. simultaneously should be fine since they're separate directories. One concern: disk space and time. 4 Next.js projects with node_modules... that's fine typically. Also, should I use `create-next-app`? A cleaner approach for templates is to write the files manually and use a minimal npm install. Actually `create-next-app` generates a lot of boilerplate; for 4 projects, writing manually with specific configs might be more controlled. But agents can decide. I'll give them clear instructions. Let me also decide versions: - Next.js 14 (as specified) - React 18 - Tailwind CSS 3.x (Tailwind 4 changed config approach; user said Tailwind CSS, and Next.js 14 pairs well with Tailwind 3.4) - Framer Motion for SaaS landing - Recharts for analytics chart - SQLite: better-sqlite3 (sync, simple) - but Next.js serverless... for Next 14 with app router, better-sqlite3 works in Node runtime. Need node runtime config for API routes. Design system tokens to share: - Colors as given - Spacing tokens 8px base - Typography: let's define a clean font system - maybe serif display for restaurant (like Fraunces or Playfair), sans for others? User said consistent design system. I'll use a consistent approach: maybe "Georgia/Source Serif" for restaurant headers and Inter for everything else. Actually to keep consistent, let's use a single font family stack: Inter for body, plus a display serif for headings across all 4 to give them the premium "portfolio-grade" feel. Hmm, but the design system should be consistent. Let me use: - Display/headings: "Fraunces" serif (via next/font or Google Fonts) — adds editorially premium feel - Body: Inter or system sans Actually, to keep fonts minimal and consistent, maybe use a Google font via next/font. But static export with next/font works fine (it inlines fonts). Let me have each project use next/font/google with Inter + Fraunces. Careful: next/font with static export works. Alternatively use system font stacks to avoid dependency on Google Fonts at build time (network needed). next/font/google downloads fonts at build time - requires network. Agent machines usually have network. It's fine. Let me define the shared design system: ``` Colors: --bg-primary: #ffffff --bg-secondary: #f4efe8 --text-primary: #1a1a1a --text-secondary: #6b6b6b --brand: #5a4a42 --border: #e0ddd8 --error: #c94a4a Spacing (8px base): xs=4px, sm=8px, md=16px, lg=24px, xl=32px, 2xl=48px, 3xl=64px Typography: Display: Fraunces serif Body: Inter sans ``` Tailwind config extensions: ```js colors: { bg: { primary: '#ffffff', secondary: '#f4efe8' }, text: { primary: '#1a1a1a', secondary: '#6b6b6b' }, brand: '#5a4a42', border: { DEFAULT: '#e0ddd8' }, error: '#c94a4a', // brand shades 'brand-50': ..., etc. } spacing: { xs: '4px', sm: '8px', md: '16px', lg: '24px', xl: '32px', '2xl': '48px', '3xl': '64px' } ``` I should create a shared design-tokens.md doc and maybe a README at the root explaining the portfolio. Portfolio root: /home/daniel/template-sites with 4 subfolders: - restaurant-site/ (frontend static) - taskflow-saas/ (frontend static) — user called it "SaaS Dashboard Landing" with concept TaskFlow - booking-system/ (backend) - analytics-dashboard/ (backend) Let me name folders simply: `01-restaurant`, `02-taskflow-saas`, `03-booking-system`, `04-analytics-dashboard`. Or cleaner names: `restaurant-site`, `saas-landing`, `booking-system`, `analytics-dashboard`. I'll go with clean names. Now the plan. Let me create PLAN.md first, then delegate. Regarding whether agents can verify builds: yes, agents have bash access. Each agent should run `npm install` and `npm run build` to verify. For the backend ones, run `npm run dev` briefly? Hard to verify dev server in agent context but they can hit API routes via curl after starting dev server in background, or use `next build` + start. For backend verification, they can: - `npm run build` - start `npm run start` in background, curl /api/bookings, then kill OK let me draft everything. Actually — first, let me check the directory. Also check node/npm versions available. Let me start. I'll do Phase 1: check environment, then Phase 2: PLAN.md, then Phase 3: delegate 4 agents in parallel (Task tool, general type), then Phase 4: verify builds myself. For the agent prompts, I need to be VERY detailed since each agent starts fresh. I'll include: - Full design systems tokens - Complete page/component list - Behavior requirements - Tech constraints - Verification instructions - What to return Let me write out the detailed spec per site. **Site 1: Restaurant Site (static export)** - Folder: `/home/daniel/template-sites/restaurant-site` - Next.js 14 + Tailwind CSS 3.4, static export (`output: 'export'`) - Brand: Ember & Wood - Content sections: Logo, sticky nav (hamburger on mobile), hero, about (2-col), featured dishes (3-col grid), gallery (lightbox), testimonials, hours/contact, reservation CTA (link to phone or scroll), footer - UX: smooth scroll (CSS scroll-behavior / JS), image lazy loading, hover animations, lightbox gallery (custom, no external libs), no API calls - Images: use placeholder images. Since no API calls and no external image host reliance, use local SVG placeholders or picsum? For static templates, nice to have engaging images. Options: use `/images/*.svg` generated inline (illustrations) or use images.unsplash.com URLs directly in . User wants lazy loading + production quality. Unsplash hotlinks in with loading="lazy" work but require network. Better: generate tasteful SVG placeholder images locally so it's self-contained. Agents can create SVG assets (food illustrations, gallery). Let me instruct agents to create local SVG placeholders in public/images with brand-appropriate colors/design, OR use `next/image` with local SVG. Simpler: plain with local SVGs and lazy loading. Actually for a "polished" portfolio, custom SVGs are the safest offline approach. Hmm, but real photos look better for a restaurant. A hybrid: use Unsplash source URLs with proper alt text? That breaks offline and the "no broken links" requirement could fail at review time if offline... but reviewer will be online probably. Still, hotlinking is fragile. I'll go with locally-generated SVG placeholders that look designed (not gray boxes). This shows off brand design and is 100% self-contained. I can describe to the agent to create appealing minimal-graphic SVG images (e.g., a plate composition, ember tones). Actually, let me reconsider: I can create nice "duotone" SVG images with the brand palette — like abstract food photography placeholders. These are fine. **Site 2: TaskFlow SaaS Landing (static export)** - Folder: `/home/daniel/template-sites/taskflow-saas` - Next.js 14 + Tailwind 3.4 + Framer Motion, static export - Sections: Hero (with animated headline), features (3-col grid), interactive task widget demo (add, complete, delete with useState), pricing (3 tiers), testimonials, CTA footer - Fully interactive widget; localStorage persistence optional (nice touch); Framer Motion for enter/exit animations - Animate with respect to prefers-reduced-motion (useReducedMotion) **Site 3: Restaurant Booking System (full-stack, SQLite)** - Folder: `/home/daniel/template-sites/booking-system` - Next.js 14 full-stack, React, SQLite (better-sqlite3) - Public: hero, about, booking widget (date, time, party size, guest info), testimonials, contact - Admin: `/admin` route. Login (password from env `ADMIN_PASSWORD`, default). Table of bookings with actions: confirm, mark done, delete - API: `/api/bookings` GET, POST, DELETE, PATCH. Validation: no past dates, no overlaps (same table/time), required fields - DB: `booking.db` file-based via better-sqlite3, seed with sample bookings (seed script `npm run seed`) - .env.example, README with setup steps - Node runtime for API routes (`export const runtime = 'nodejs'`) **Site 4: Analytics Dashboard (full-stack, SQLite)** - Folder: `/home/daniel/template-sites/analytics-dashboard` - Next.js 14 full-stack, React, SQLite (better-sqlite3) - Concept: Metrics — content analytics dashboard - Dashboard: 3 metric cards (views, engagement, active), feed of content items updating every 5s, right sidebar trending topics, click item → detail page with chart - Routes: /dashboard (main), /settings (theme toggle, polling freq), /analytics (7-day overview) - API: /api/metrics, /api/feed, /api/content/[id]. Backend updates views/engagement every 5s (interval in server? tricky with Next — better to update on each feed request + a server-side tick. Implementation: in-memory interval started in the API route module scope that bumps metrics every 5s and persists to SQLite. When dev server runs, interval runs. That works for a dev/demo template. Alternatively update values deterministically on each GET based on elapsed time — simpler and stateless. I'll suggest: on each /api/feed GET, increment views/engagement slightly and write back, plus update a running "active users" number. This gives live-updating feel without global intervals and works across requests. For detail chart, generate 7-day history deterministic per content id.) - Chart: Recharts line chart (7-day performance) - Seed 15-20 sample content items - Theme toggle (light/dark) — design system still consistent; dark mode derived from tokens - Polling frequency setting (localStorage + context) Both backend sites: consistent design system, accessible, responsive. Also root README describing all 4 + how to run. And PLAN.md tracking. Consideration: Next.js 14 requires React 18.3. Fine. better-sqlite3 is a native module — needs compilation at install. Should be OK on this Linux env. Alternative: sql.js or node:sqlite? Node 22 has built-in `node:sqlite`! Let me check node version. If Node 22+, `node:sqlite` avoids native deps entirely. But better-sqlite3 is more familiar/standard. I'll check the environment first. If Node 22, I could still use better-sqlite3 (it supports Node 22). Let me just check. Spacing scale (Tailwind extended spacing, 8px base): xs: 4px, sm: 8px, md: 16px, lg: 24px, xl: 32px, 2xl: 48px, 3xl: 64px Typography: Display font: Fraunces (via next/font/google, fallback Georgia serif) for headings Body font: Inter (via next/font/google, fallback system sans) for body/UI Type scale: hero 4xl-5xl, section titles 3xl, cards xl, body md, caption sm Border radius: rounded-sm for small, rounded-md (8px), rounded-xl (16px) — consistent: use rounded-xl for cards, rounded-full for buttons/pills (44px min touch target). # Plan: MoshineSites Portfolio — 4 Site Templates

## Objective
Generate 4 production-grade, portfolio-ready site templates in separate subfolders, sharing one consistent design system. Frontend-only sites are statically exported; backend sites are full-stack Next.js with API routes + SQLite.

## Milestones

### M1: Shared Design System + Scaffolding
- Scope: Design tokens (colors, spacing, typography), root docs
- Deliverables: `PLAN.md`, `README.md`, `design-system.md`
- Tasks:
  - [x] Define tokens (colors, spacing scale, type scale, radii, shadows)
  - [x] Document responsive + accessibility requirements

### M2: Frontend-Only Sites (static export)
- Scope: `restaurant-site` (Ember & Wood), `taskflow-saas` (TaskFlow)
- Deliverables: Build passes `output: 'export'` → `out/` for both
- Tasks:
  - [ ] Agent A: restaurant-site complete (nav, hero, about, dishes, gallery, testimonials, hours/contact, footer) + local SVG images + lightbox
  - [ ] Agent B: taskflow-saas complete (hero, features, interactive task widget, pricing, testimonials, CTA) + Framer Motion
  - [ ] Verify static exports

### M3: Backend-Hosted Sites (full-stack)
- Scope: `booking-system` (Ember & Wood booking), `analytics-dashboard` (Metrics)
- Deliverables: API routes working, SQLite seeded, builds pass
- Tasks:
  - [ ] Agent C: booking-system (public booking widget, /admin, /api/bookings CRUD + validation, seed)
  - [ ] Agent D: analytics-dashboard (/dashboard, /settings, /analytics, /api/metrics + /feed + /content/[id], live updates, Recharts)
  - [ ] Verify APIs via curl + seeded data

### M4: Verification & Polish
- Scope: Builds, API smoke tests, responsive/accessibility review
- Tasks:
  - [ ] Run `npm run build` for all 4
  - [ ] Smoke-test backend APIs
  - [ ] Fix any console errors / broken links
  - [ ] Final screenshots for refinement

## Implementation Orchestration
1. Scaffold each site independently (Next.js 14 pin, Tailwind 3.4, TypeScript)
2. Agents build in parallel in isolated folders
3. Shared design tokens applied via Tailwind theme + CSS variables in every site
4. Verify: `npm run build` (static export for M2; full build for M3), API curl tests
5. Review with webapp-testing / screenshots for refinement

## Momentum
- **now**: Launch 4 parallel build agents
- **next**: Verify builds + APIs
- **blocked**: —
- **improve**: Screenshot review pass for polish

# MoshineSites Template Portfolio — Design System

One consistent design system across all 4 templates.

## Colors (CSS variables + Tailwind theme)

| Token | Value | Purpose |
|-------|-------|---------|
| `--bg-primary` | `#ffffff` | Page background |
| `--bg-secondary` | `#f4efe8` | Alternating sections, cards |
| `--text-primary` | `#1a1a1a` | Headings / body (AA on white & secondary bg) |
| `--text-secondary` | `#6b6b6b` | Muted text (AA on white & #f4efe8) |
| `--brand` | `#5a4a42` | Brand color (AA on white) |
| `--border` | `#e0ddd8` | Hairlines, dividers |
| `--error` | `#c94a4a` | Errors (AA on white) |

### Derived brand scale (from `#5a4a42`)
`brand-50 #faf8f6`, `brand-100 #f0ece8`, `brand-200 #ddd4cd`, `brand-300 #c4b7ae`, `brand-400 #a98f82`, `brand-500 #5a4a42`, `brand-600 #4a3d37`, `brand-700 #3b312c`, `brand-800 #2c2521`, `brand-900 #1d1815`

Supporting: `success #3d7a4e`, `warning #b07d2b`

## Spacing (8px base → Tailwind `extend.spacing`)

`xs: 4px`, `sm: 8px`, `md: 16px`, `lg: 24px`, `xl: 32px`, `2xl: 48px`, `3xl: 64px`

## Typography

- **Display:** Fraunces (serif, via `next/font/google`, fallback Georgia) — headings, hero, section titles
- **Body:** Inter (sans, via `next/font/google`, fallback system-ui) — body, UI, forms
- Scale: hero `text-4xl`–`text-5xl`, section titles `text-3xl`, cards `text-xl`, body `text-md`, captions `text-sm`

## Radii & Shadows

- Cards `rounded-xl` (16px), pills/buttons `rounded-full`, inputs `rounded-md`
- Soft shadows: `0 1px 2px rgba(26,26,26,.04)`, `0 4px 12px rgba(26,26,26,.06)`

## Responsive

- Mobile 0–640px: 1 column, hamburger nav
- Tablet 640–1024px: 2 columns (`sm:` breakpoint)

Good picture of booking-system. Current state vs enhanced spec:

Matches already:
- SQLite + seed + DB created
- API CRUD + admin login/logout with HMAC cookie
- Validation (no past dates, party 1-12, covers capacity)
- Widget with inline errors, success state, loading presumably
- Admin table presumably

Gaps vs ENHANCED spec:
1. Time slots: spec says lunch 11:00-12:30 (15-min intervals), dinner 17:00-21:00. Current: lunch 12:00-13:30, dinner 18:00-20:30. → Update LIB (ALLOWED_TIMES) + widget dropdown + re-seed to match. Note the seeded DB has old times; re-seed needed (or seed regenerates with new slots).
2. Party size: spec says dropdown 1-8 with labels ("Just me", "2 people"...). Current: 1-12. → Update validation to 1-12 or 1-8? Spec says "Party size: dropdown 1-8 people (show labels)". The DB check constraint says 1-12. The validation says 1-12. Hmm — the enhanced spec says 1-8. Should I change to 1-8? The original prompt said 1-12; the new spec explicitly says 1-8 people with labels. Follow the latest: update to 1-8 with labels, update DB constraint... changing constraint requires recreating table (or keep constraint 1-12 which is a superset — validation 1-8 still enforced app-level; DB constraint at 1-12 doesn't conflict). Cleaner: keep DB CHECK 1-12 (superset, doesn't hurt) but validate UI/server at 1-8 with labels. Actually to be precise and consistent, change server validation to 1-8 and keep DB check at 1-12 (superset) — that's fine and avoids table migration. Hmm, but "consistency": the constraint says BETWEEN 1 AND 12 — a 9-party booking would be rejected by server anyway. Fine.
   Actually wait — re-seeding: seed.cjs inserts bookings; those use party sizes. Also capacity per slot 24 covers with max party 8... fine.
3. Success banner: spec says "Reservation confirmed for [date] at [time]. Confirmation email sent to [email]" dismissible, auto-disappear after 4s. Current success card is a full card "Thank you {name}. We'll confirm your table..." — needs rework to green banner with exact copy + dismiss button + auto-dismiss 4s.
4. Hero: spec says headline "Reserve your table", subheadline, large CTA. Current hero is "Ember & Wood" brand hero. Need to check — enhanced spec wants hero with "Reserve your table". I'll instruct: hero headline "Reserve your table" (can keep brand intro), CTA to booking widget.
5. Nav links: Home, Menu, Bookings, Contact + hamburger on mobile. Current nav.tsx — need to check; likely has some links. Agent should verify/align.
6. About 2-col fade-in on scroll: need an About section with text left, image right, fade-in on scroll (IntersectionObserver or framer-lite CSS). Current page.tsx head didn't show About — need to check. Agent should add.
7. Admin table: columns Date, Time, Party Size, Guest Name, Phone, Email, Status, Actions; badges pending amber/confirmed green/completed gray/cancelled red; statuses names — current lib uses 'done' but spec uses 'completed'. Must rename 'done' → 'completed' everywhere (db.ts constraint, lib, admin dashboard, NEXT_STATUSES). That requires re-seeding (constraint check will reject 'completed' if table already exists with old constraint!). getDb creates table if not exists — the existing booking.db already has CHECK with 'done'. The CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS won't update the existing table. So the agent must either drop/recreate booking.db (delete data/booking.db*) or ALTER (SQLite can't easily alter constraints). Simplest: delete data/booking.db* and re-run seed. Instruct agent to do that.
8. Delete action row: spec says delete with modal confirmation. Current admin — need check; agent should ensure modal confirm.
9. Alternate row backgrounds, sticky table header, responsive collapse to cards on mobile, real-time immediate reflection.
10. Testimonials 3 cards, hover lift — exists.
11. Hours + contact 2-col — likely exists (page.tsx had hours data).
12. Time dropdown with 15-min intervals: lunch 11:00-12:30 → 11:00, 11:15, 11:30, 11:45, 12:00, 12:15, 12:30 (7 slots); dinner 17:00-21:00 → 17:00..21:00 in 15-min increments = 17 slots. That's 24 slots total. The "2 hours notice for today" validation still applies.
    Wait: spec says lunch 11:00–12:30, dinner 17:00–21:00. So last dinner 21:00. OK.

Also check: seed.cjs uses old times and status 'done' → agent must update seed to new slots/status, then delete old DB and re-run seed.

Also "show calendar on focus" for date input — minor, native date input shows calendar. Fine.

Also menu link: there's no menu section; nav link "Menu" could scroll to a featured dishes section? Hmm, the booking system doesn't have a menu section per spec (it has hero, about, widget, testimonials, hours/contact). "Menu" link target — maybe anchor to about? Or the enhanced spec just says nav links (Home, Menu, Bookings, Contact). I'll let the agent map Menu → a small "menu/press" note or reuse About as "Menu"? Better: add a tiny "Menu" section (3 signature items list) or just point Menu → #about? Cleanest: nav links Home (#top), Menu (#hours?) no. Let me just instruct: Menu anchors to a compact signature dishes strip (#menu) — small 3-item list, cheap to add, makes nav honest. Or simpler: drop Menu link... but spec explicit. I'll add tiny signature-dishes strip.

OK. Now the plan for the two agents:

Agent C2 (booking-system finish): detailed instructions to review current code, apply the ENHANCED spec deltas, rebuild DB, verify everything, produce report.

Agent D2 (ecommerce-store fresh build): full spec as given plus backend design + design system + verify.

Let me also think about e-commerce backend details to specify:

Folder: /home/daniel/template-sites/ecommerce-store
Stack: Next 14.2 pinned, React 18, TS, Tailwind 3.4, better-sqlite3, nodejs runtime APIs. NO UI libs. Recharts not needed here. Single design system from design-system.md.

DB: data/store.db
Tables:
- products(id INTEGER PK, name, slug UNIQUE, description, price_cents INTEGER, category TEXT, image TEXT (SVG path), stock INTEGER, rating REAL, created_at)
- categories: just distinct product.category or a categories table. Simpler: store category TEXT on product; GET /api/products?category= filters.
- orders(id INTEGER PK, order_number TEXT UNIQUE (e.g. ORD-<uppercase>), customer_name, email, phone, address_line, city, state, zip, status TEXT ('placed','shipped','cancelled'), subtotal_cents, shipping_cents, tax_cents, total_cents, created_at)
- order_items(id, order_id FK, product_id, name, unit_price_cents, qty, line_total_cents)
- reviews? Spec: "Optional: star rating, 2-3 dummy reviews" — make reviews part of product card (rating), and detail page shows rating + 2-3 dummy reviews hardcoded per product (not DB) OR tiny reviews table. Keep simple: products.rating + reviews as static sample data in product detail component (non-DB) — acceptable per "dummy reviews". Hmm, "production-grade" would prefer DB, but dummy is explicitly optional/simplified. I'll keep rating on product + 2-3 dummy reviews in component data (deterministic per product).

API routes:
- GET /api/products?category=&q=&page=&pageSize=12 → { items, total, page, pageSize, totalPages, categories }
- GET /api/products/[id] → product (or by slug)
- GET /api/categories → distinct categories
- POST /api/orders (create order from cart + shipping; validates stock, computes totals server-side: subtotal, shipping (free over $100 else $8 flat), tax 8.5%; decrements stock; creates order + items; returns order with number)
- GET /api/orders → list (admin)
- GET /api/orders/[id] → detail (public: by order number? admin list) — public confirmation page uses order number: GET /api/orders/[orderNumber] lookup... store order_number; page /order/[orderId] where orderId is the order number string.
- PATCH /api/orders/[id] (admin: mark shipped, cancel)
- Admin products CRUD: GET/POST /api/admin/products, PATCH/DELETE /api/admin/products/[id] (admin-gated); or fold into /api/products with admin cookie check for POST/PATCH/DELETE. Cleaner: /api/admin/products for mutations; /api/products read-only public. I'll spec /api/admin/products.
- POST /api/admin/login, POST /api/admin/logout (same HMAC cookie auth pattern as booking — reuse approach from booking lib/auth.ts; agent may copy adapted).

Cart: React context + reducer, persisted in localStorage. Cart page reads from context. Qty +/- with min 1 max stock. Add to cart triggers "Added ✓" for 1.5s + animate to cart icon (simple translate/fade via CSS; respects reduced motion). Cart badge count on nav.

Products data: 9-12 is plenty? Spec says "Load 12 products per page" → seed at least 14-18 products so pagination shows more than one page? Spec: "Load 12 products per page, pagination below". Seed 16 products → 2 pages. Good. Categories: e.g., Furniture, Lighting, Textiles, Tableware, Decor (boutique home goods vibe consistent with brand tone). Images: local SVG product illustrations in public/images/products/ (consistent designed SVGs, no external URLs). Coming from a designer brand, rendered as styled SVGs — consistent with the rest of portfolio. Agent with SVG skill can produce tasteful product illustrations (chair, lamp, vase, throw, candle, etc.). This is significant work (16 SVGs). Instruct 4-6 reusable SVG product visuals with color variants to keep scope sane: e.g., 6 base illustrations (chair, lamp, vase, candle, textile, cup) reused across 16 products with palette variations. That's clever and keeps quality.

Admin pages:
- /admin → dashboard: 3-4 metric cards (total orders, revenue, items sold, avg order value) + recent orders table preview
- /admin/orders → full orders table (date, customer, total, status badges, actions view/mark shipped/cancel; row click → detail? spec: "Click row → detail page" — order detail could be a drawer or /admin/orders/[id] page. I'll do /admin/orders/[id] page.)
- /admin/products → table (name, price, stock, actions) + "Add product" button; add/edit modal form (name, price, description, stock, image select from existing SVGs, category); delete with confirm.
- /admin/settings → logout + general settings (store name display?) — keep simple: logout + about text.
- Sidebar nav collapsible on mobile.

Auth: same cookie approach. Admin layout wraps pages with server guard redirecting to login form. Reuse pattern from booking-system.

Public pages:
- / (home): hero "Shop our collection", CTA browse → /shop, featured products (top rated 4)
- /shop: nav (Logo, Shop, About? Contact?) — spec nav: Shop, About, Contact + cart icon with badge. Hero headline "Shop our collection". Search input (client filters via API q), category dropdown, price range slider (optional — include simple max budget slider? spec optional; skip or include simple one. I'll make it optional: implement category + search; price filter as a simple max-price slider — it's "optional" so agent may include if cheap. I'll say optional/nice-to-have.)
- Product grid 3-col desktop, 2 tablet, 1 mobile; card: image, name, price brand bold, description 1-2 lines, "View details" button; hover: card elevates, image zoom, button darkens. Pagination below (12/page). Click card or View details → /product/[id].
- /product/[id]: 2-col desktop image left / details right, stacked mobile; main image + 3-4 thumbnails swapping main; name h1, price large bold brand, stock status ("In stock" green / "Out of stock" gray); description 2-3 paragraphs (use product.description split or generate); quantity selector minus/plus + number input min 1 max stock; "Add to cart" full-width primary, on click "Added ✓" 1.5s + animate; star rating + 2-3 dummy reviews; related products 3-col grid same card style (same category, exclude self, up to 3).
- /cart: table (thumbnail, name, qty +/- , unit price, line total, remove X); summary sticky right (subtotal, shipping flat/free, tax, total bold) + "Proceed to checkout" + "Continue shopping"; empty state.
- /checkout: 2-col form left (Billing: name/email/phone; Shipping: street/city/state/zip; Payment mock: card/exp/cvv text inputs no real validation) + order summary right (items thumbnails qty price; subtotal/shipping/tax/total); all fields required validated inline; "Place order" full width with "Processing..." loading; error red banner "Something went wrong. - /order/[orderId] (orderNumber): success ✓ green badge large, order number, order date, estimated delivery date (e.g., +5 days), customer info, items table, totals, "Continue shopping" button.

Consistent design system everywhere; skip link; focus rings; reduced motion; 44px targets; lazy images; semantic HTML; responsive.

// Client-safe money + date formatting helpers (NO node imports).
export const TAX_RATE = 0.085;
export const SHIPPING_FLAT_CENTS = 800;
export const FREE_SHIPPING_THRESHOLD_CENTS = 10000;

export function formatCents(cents: number): string {
  return `$${(cents / 100).toFixed(2)}`;
}

export function computeShipping(subtotalCents: number): number {
  return subtotalCents >= FREE_SHIPPING_THRESHOLD_CENTS ? 0 : SHIPPING_FLAT_CENTS;
}

export function computeTax(subtotalCents: number): number {
  return Math.round(subtotalCents * TAX_RATE);
}

export function computeTotals(subtotalCents: number) {
  const shipping = computeShipping(subtotalCents);
  const tax = computeTax(subtotalCents);
  return { subtotal: subtotalCents, shipping, tax, total: subtotalCents + shipping + tax };
}

input.content:
# Northlight Goods — Full-Stack E-Commerce Store

A complete, portfolio-grade e-commerce template built with **Next.js 14 (App Router) + SQLite**. Catalog, cart, checkout, order confirmation, and a full admin panel — all wired to a real backend with zero external UI libraries.

## Features

- **Storefront**
  - `/` — home with hero + featured products
  - `/shop` — search, category filter, 12-per-page pagination
  - `/product/[id]` — image gallery, quantity selector, add to cart, reviews, related products
  - `/cart` — client cart (React context + `localStorage`), quantity controls, live totals
  - `/checkout` — validated billing / shipping / mock payment form, order summary
  - `/order/[orderId]` — order confirmation with estimated delivery
- **Admin panel** (`/admin`, password protected)
  - Dashboard with revenue / orders / items-sold / average order value metrics
  - Orders: view, mark shipped, cancel (with restock) — updates instantly, no reload
  - Products: add / edit (modal form) / delete (confirm dialog)
  - Settings: logout + store defaults
- **Backend**
  - SQLite (`data/store.db`, file-based, WAL mode)
  - API routes (all Node runtime): products, orders, categories, admin auth, admin product CRUD
  - Seeded with 16 products across 5 categories + 3 sample orders
  - Consistent pricing rules shared between storefront and server (free shipping over $100, flat $8, 8.5% tax)

## Setup

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env   # optional — defaults are fine for local dev
npm run seed           # creates data/store.db and seeds products + sample orders
npm run dev            # http://localhost:3020
```

## Production

```bash
npm run build && npm run start
```

## Admin access

- URL: `http://localhost:3020/admin`
- Password: `ADMIN_PASSWORD` env var — default `admin123` (change it before deploying)

## API summary

| Method | Route | Auth | Purpose |
| ------ | ----- | ---- | ------- |
| GET | `/api/products` | — | List with `category`, `q`, `page`, `pageSize` |
| GET | `/api/products/:id` | — | Single product |
| GET | `/api/categories` | — | Distinct categories |
| POST | `/api/orders` | — | Place an order (validates stock, decrements, computes totals) |
| GET | `/api/orders` | admin | List orders with items |
| GET | `/api/orders/:id` | admin | Order detail |
| PATCH | `/api/orders/:id` | admin | Mark shipped / cancel (cancel restocks) |
| POST | `/api/admin/products` | admin | Create product |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/products/:id` | admin | Update product |
| DELETE | `/api/admin/products/:id` | admin | Delete product |
| POST | `/api/admin/login` / `logout` | — | Admin session (httpOnly cookie) |

## Design system

Uses the shared MoshineSites design system (`/design-system.md` at the portfolio root): brand `#5a4a42`, Fraunces + Inter, 8px spacing scale, WCAG AA contrast, 44px touch targets, `prefers-reduced-motion` support.

# Plan: MoshineSites Portfolio — 4 Site Templates (rev 3 — complete)

## Objective
4 production-grade, portfolio-ready site templates in separate subfolders, sharing one consistent design system. Frontend-only sites are statically exported; backend sites are full-stack Next.js with API routes + SQLite and fully polished frontends.

## Milestones

### M1: Shared Design System + Scaffolding ✅
- [x] Define tokens (colors, spacing scale, type scale, radii, shadows) → design-system.md
- [x] Document responsive + accessibility requirements

### M2: Frontend-Only Sites (static export) ✅ verified
- `restaurant-site` (Ember & Wood) — built, `out/` served (HTTP 200)
- `taskflow-saas` (TaskFlow) — built, `out/` served (HTTP 200)
- `start` script uses `node scripts/serve-out.mjs` (zero-dep static server) since `next start` breaks on static export

### M3: Backend-Hosted Sites (full-stack, polished frontends) ✅ verified
- `booking-system` (Ember & Wood booking) — enhanced frontend (slots 11:00-12:30/17:00-21:00 15-min, party 1-8 labels, statuses pending/confirmed/completed/cancelled, capacity 24, admin table + delete modal, success banner auto-dismiss, About fade-in), SQLite, admin auth; agent-verified E2E
- `ecommerce-store` (Northlight Goods, replaces analytics-dashboard per client direction) — full storefront + admin, manually completed & smoke-tested (below)
- `analytics-dashboard` removed from portfolio

### M4: Verification & Polish ✅
- [x] `npm run build` for all 4 sites (restaurant, taskflow, booking, ecommerce) — all pass
- [x] API smoke tests: ecommerce (products list/filter/search/pagination, categories, order placement + stock decrement + free-shipping threshold, admin auth + order status + product CRUD, 401/400/404/409 edge cases) — all pass
- [x] Static sites served via `scripts/serve-out.mjs` — 200 OK
- [x] Re-seeded ecommerce `data/store.db` to clean 16 products / 3 orders after testing
- [x] Root README + final PLAN.md status

## Ecommerce build detail (manual completion)
- Stage 1 (done): server foundation — `lib/{db,store,auth}.ts`, `lib/seed.cjs`, all `/api/...` routes, cart provider, site chrome/nav/footer/product-card/stars, 11 product SVGs, seeded DB
- Stage 2 (done, manual — two delegated agents returned empty): public pages `/`, `/shop`, `/product/[id]`, `/cart`, `/checkout`, `/order/[orderId]`; admin pages `/admin/login`, dashboard, orders list/detail, products CRUD, settings; `/api/admin/products` + `[id]` routes; `confirm-dialog.tsx`, `status-badge.tsx`, `admin-shell.tsx`; README.md
- Client-safe pricing/search constants moved to `lib/{format,catalog}.ts` so `@/lib/*` alias resolves and only type-safe intent crosses the client boundary
- Verification: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `next build` passes (21 routes), full curl suite green

## How to run

| Site | Folder | Command | URL |
| ---- | ------ | ------- | --- |
| Restaurant | `restaurant-site` | `npm run build && npm start` | http://localhost:3000 |

# MoshineSites — Portfolio of Site Templates

Four production-grade, portfolio-ready site templates in one repo, each a self-contained project sharing one design system.

## The templates

| # | Template | Folder | Type | Stack |
|---|----------|--------|------|-------|
| 1 | **Ember & Wood** — restaurant | `restaurant-site` | Static export | Next.js, Tailwind, 17 hand-drawn SVGs |

All four sites follow `design-system.md`: brand `#5a4a42`, Fraunces + Inter type pairing, an 8px spacing scale, WCAG AA contrast, 44px touch targets, and mobile → tablet → desktop responsiveness.

Each folder is standalone:

```bash

cd restaurant-site && npm install && npm run build && npm start   # http://localhost:3000
cd taskflow-saas   && npm install && npm run build && npm start   # http://localhost:3001

## Backend notes

- Both backend sites use SQLite (file-based, seeded via `npm run seed`) with hand-rolled API routes — no framework DB layer, no external UI libraries.

All four sites: `npm run build` green. Ecommerce + booking API suites exercised against running servers (auth, CRUD, stock/capacity edge cases). See `PLAN.md` for the full status.

# MoshineSites Template Portfolio — Design System

One consistent design system across all 4 templates.

## Colors (CSS variables + Tailwind theme)

| Token | Value | Purpose |
|-------|-------|---------|
| `--bg-primary` | `#ffffff` | Page background |
| `--bg-secondary` | `#f4efe8` | Alternating sections, cards |
| `--text-primary` | `#1a1a1a` | Headings / body (AA on white & secondary bg) |
| `--text-secondary` | `#6b6b6b` | Muted text (AA on white & #f4efe8) |
| `--brand` | `#5a4a42` | Brand color (AA on white) |
| `--border` | `#e0ddd8` | Hairlines, dividers |
| `--error` | `#c94a4a` | Errors (AA on white) |

### Derived brand scale (from `#5a4a42`)
`brand-50 #faf8f6`, `brand-100 #f0ece8`, `brand-200 #ddd4cd`, `brand-300 #c4b7ae`, `brand-400 #a98f82`, `brand-500 #5a4a42`, `brand-600 #4a3d37`, `brand-700 #3b312c`, `brand-800 #2c2521`, `brand-900 #1d1815`

Supporting: `success #3d7a4e`, `warning #b07d2b`

## Spacing (8px base → Tailwind `extend.spacing`)

`xs: 4px`, `sm: 8px`, `md: 16px`, `lg: 24px`, `xl: 32px`, `2xl: 48px`, `3xl: 64px`

## Typography

- **Display:** Fraunces (serif, via `next/font/google`, fallback Georgia) — headings, hero, section titles
- **Body:** Inter (sans, via `next/font/google`, fallback system-ui) — body, UI, forms
- Scale: hero `text-4xl`–`text-5xl`, section titles `text-3xl`, cards `text-xl`, body `text-md`, captions `text-sm`

## Radii & Shadows

- Cards `rounded-xl` (16px), pills/buttons `rounded-full`, inputs `rounded-md`
- Soft shadows: `0 1px 2px rgba(26,26,26,.04)`, `0 4px 12px rgba(26,26,26,.06)`

## Responsive

- Mobile 0–640px: 1 column, hamburger nav
- Tablet 640–1024px: 2 columns (`sm:` breakpoint)
- Desktop 1024px+: 3 columns (`lg:` breakpoint)

## Accessibility (all templates)

- WCAG AA: 4.5:1 contrast minimum; headings/body as tokenized above
- 44px minimum touch targets (buttons, links, inputs)
- Semantic HTML5 landmarks (`header`, `nav`, `main`, `section`, `footer`)
- `focus-visible` ring: 2px brand, 2px offset
- `prefers-reduced-motion` respected (CSS media query + `useReducedMotion`)
- `aria-label`s on icon-only controls; form labels associated with inputs
- Decorative images `alt=""`; content images descriptive `alt`

## Tech Baseline

- Next.js **14.2.x** (pin), React 18, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS **3.4.x**
- No external UI component libraries
- Frontend-only: `output: 'export'` in next.config, no API calls, local SVG image assets
- Backend: `better-sqlite3`, `export const runtime = 'nodejs'` on API routes, seed script, `.env.example`, README
- Fast: lazy-loaded images, minimal deps, no console errors

Good. Since `prefers-reduced-motion` is already handled globally in globals.css (the media query kills all animations), I don't need per-element detection. The inline fade-in animation will be suppressed by the CSS media query.

32:   const [pollFreq, setPollFreqState] = useState<PollFreq>(5000);
33: 
34:   // Init from storage (client only).
35:   useEffect(() => {
36:     try {
37:       const t = window.localStorage.getItem(THEME_KEY) as Theme | null;
38:       if (t === 'light' || t === 'dark' || t === 'system') setThemeState(t);
39:       const p = Number(window.localStorage.getItem(POLL_KEY));
40:       if (p === 3000 || p === 5000 || p === 10000 || p === 0) setPollFreqState(p as PollFreq);
41:     } catch {

43:     }
44:   }, []);

49:     const onChange = () => { if (theme === 'system') applyTheme('system'); };
50:     mq.addEventListener('change', onChange);
51:     return () => mq.removeEventListener('change', onChange);
52:   }, [theme]);
53: 
54:   const setTheme = (t: Theme) => {
55:     setThemeState(t);
56:     try {
57:       window.localStorage.setItem(THEME_KEY, t);
58:     } catch { /* ignore */ }
59:   };
60: 
61:   const setPollFreq = (n: PollFreq) => {
62:     setPollFreqState(n);
63:     try {
64:       window.localStorage.setItem(POLL_KEY, String(n));
65:     } catch { /* ignore */ }
66:   };
67: 
68:   const value = useMemo(
69:     () => ({ theme, setTheme, pollFreq, setPollFreq }),
70:     [theme, pollFreq]
71:   );
72: 
73:   return <SettingsContext.Provider value={value}>{children}</SettingsContext.Provider>;
74: }

input.content:
# Analytics Dashboard (MetricsApp)

A TweetDeck-style social analytics template, part of the template-sites collection.
Next.js 14 + SQLite (better-sqlite3) + Recharts, with a lightweight live simulator
so the numbers visibly move without any external services.

## Features

- **/dashboard** — three metric cards (Views, Engagement, Active now) with
  day-over-day deltas, a polling live feed of content posts, and a trending-topics sidebar.
- **/analytics** — 7-day aggregate views + engagement area chart (Recharts) plus
  "best posting day" and "highest engagement rate" highlights.
- **/content/[id]** — full post detail: metadata, tags, stat cards, and a 7-day
  performance chart per post.
- **/settings** — light / dark / system theme and polling interval
  (3s / 5s / 10s / paused). Preferences persist in localStorage.
- **Live simulation** — a background ticker bumps views/engagement on 3 random posts
  every 5 seconds (configurable), so dashboards behave like real analytics products.
- Dark mode via `class` strategy; accessible (skip link, ARIA labels, reduced-motion
  support, 44px touch targets).

## API

| Route                  | Description                                      |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `GET /api/metrics`     | Totals, 7-day series, trending topics            |
| `GET /api/feed`        | Up to 50 content items, newest first             |
| `GET /api/content/:id` | Single content item + its 7-day daily stats      |

All responses use the envelope `{ ok: boolean, data?, error? }`.

## Getting started

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env        # optional; defaults work out of the box
npm run seed                # creates data/analytics.db with 18 content items
npm run dev                 # http://localhost:3000
```

To change the simulation cadence (milliseconds, min 1000, 0 disables):

```bash
SIMULATOR_INTERVAL_MS=2000 npm run dev
```

## Scripts

| Script            | Purpose                                   |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `npm run dev`     | Start Next.js dev server                  |
| `npm run seed`    | Create/reset the SQLite DB with seed data |
| `npm run build`   | Production build                          |
| `npm start`       | Serve the production build                |
| `npm run typecheck` | `tsc --noEmit`                          |

## Technology choices

- **better-sqlite3** — synchronous, zero-ORM, ideal for a self-contained template.
  Database lives at `data/analytics.db` (WAL mode, ignored by git).
- **Recharts** — the only external charting library; kept purposefully minimal.
- **Next.js API routes** (`nodejs` runtime, `force-dynamic`) so the simulator is
  guaranteed to run inside the same process that serves the pages.
- **lib/ vs src/lib/** — client-safe helpers live in the root `lib/` because the
  `@/lib/*` alias targets the root `lib/` directory, not `src/`.

## Reset

```bash
rm -f data/analytics.db && npm run seed
```

# MoshineSites — Portfolio of Site Templates

Four production-grade, portfolio-ready site templates in one repo, each a self-contained project sharing one design system.

## The templates

| # | Template | Folder | Type | Stack |
|---|----------|--------|------|-------|

| 3 | **Ember & Wood Booking** — reservations | `booking-system` | Full-stack | Next.js + SQLite + API |
| 4 | **Northlight Goods** — e-commerce | `ecommerce-store` | Full-stack | Next.js + SQLite + API + admin |

All four sites follow `design-system.md`: brand `#5a4a42`, Fraunces + Inter type pairing, an 8px spacing scale, WCAG AA contrast, 44px touch targets, and mobile → tablet → desktop responsiveness.

Every seeded order that gets cancelled in the admin panel inflates inventory by its quantities (Willow Armchair, Throw, Lamp, Mug ×4, Bowl, Vase ×2, Candle — the candle is even seeded in an order while the product is "out of stock").

- **Search LIKE wildcards:** `lib/store.ts:134-137` — a query containing `%` or `_` acts as a wildcard (e.g. `?q=%` returns everything). Escape or strip `%`/`_` in `q`.

- **Admin product list capped at 48** (`src/app/admin/(panel)/products/page.tsx:49` uses the public route's `pageSize` cap) — catalogs >48 items can't be managed/edited beyond the first page.
- **Checkout payment validation is minimal by design** (`src/app/checkout/page.tsx:28-40`): past-dated expiry accepted, no Luhn; `formatCard` truncates to 16 digits (`:78`) so 19-digit cards error at 17+ digits. 2. Make the seed either decrement stock for seeded order lines or restate the intent (HIGH — invisible inventory corruption from admin cancel).
3. Add a server-side order lookup for `/order/[orderId]` (MEDIUM — currently indistinguishable from a 404 page after session loss).
4. Delete the dead code listed above; fold `isAdmin` into `lib/auth.ts`.
5. Clamp pagination server-side to `totalPages`; add login throttling; add an order idempotency key.
6. Run `prettier --write` (not configured in this repo — add it or match the consistent 2-space/single-quote style already present, which is uniform).

❌ **Needs revision** — no CRITICALs and the core transactional design is sound (parameterized SQL, atomic stock decrement, consistent totals, honest envelopes), but the reachable checkout failure for high-stock seeded items and the seed's stock/restock double-count are user-visible defects that the smoke suite's happy-path quantities would never surface, and they should be fixed before this ships as a portfolio template.

'Failed to load feed.'; setError(nextError); ``` **[MEDIUM] Mobile nav accessible names are single ambiguous letters** `src/components/site/nav.tsx:41-42` On `sm:hidden`, the accessible name becomes "D", "A", "S" — "Analytics" is announced as "A". Use a stable key and animate only the number: ```tsx
  • // stable ``` (if you want change indication, compare previous views and blink the `` via a data-attribute + CSS, keyed off a `usePrevious`.) ### LOW **[LOW] Dead code + duplicated formatting logic** `lib/format.ts:10-15` — `formatDelta` is exported but imported nowhere; `src/components/dashboard/metric-cards.tsx:11-22` re-implements both `formatNumber` and `deltaPct` privately. Drop the colors. **[LOW] Theme FOUC — white flash for dark-mode users on every load** `src/components/site/settings-context.tsx:35-52` — `applyTheme` runs in `useEffect`, after first paint. Add a small blocking inline script in `layout.tsx` `` that reads `localStorage['metrics-theme']` (and `matchMedia` for `system`) and toggles `.dark` before hydration — server HTML is theme-neutral so `suppressHydrationWarning` stays valid. **[LOW] Row-0 / prev=0 delta shows "all time"** `src/components/dashboard/metric-cards.tsx:18-29` — when yesterday is 0 and today >0, `deltaPct` returns null → card labels "all time". Misleading on a fresh DB. Keep the live region off the list container (or confine it to the numeric delta spans). **[LOW] Same platform chip styled differently in feed vs detail** `src/components/dashboard/feed.tsx:9` (has `dark:bg-brand-200 dark:text-brand-900`) vs `src/app/content/[id]/page.tsx:38` (no dark variants) — identical platform renders differently in dark mode. Add "No content yet — run `npm run seed`." (the simulator already warns server-side, but the UI shouldn't look broken). **[LOW] Triplicated client types + page coupling** `SeriesPoint`/`MetricsData` declared in `dashboard/page.tsx`, `analytics/page.tsx`, `content/[id]/page.tsx`; `feed.tsx:6` and `metric-cards.tsx:3` import types `from '@/app/dashboard/page'`. This and the inverted seed curve together are why the "vs yesterday" deltas and charts never matched the live numbers in the late evening. 2. **Fix the seed trajectory** (`ageDays = d`, anchor to calendar today) so the template demos *growth*; verify the aggregate series rises toward today after reseeding (`rm data/analytics.db && npm run seed`). 3. **Wire chart colors to the CSS vars** (`var(--text-secondary)`, `var(--border)`, `var(--brand)`) instead of hardcoded hex so dark mode is readable with zero extra JS. 4. **Tighten polling UX** — stable feed keys, honest paused-state message, error only cleared when both endpoints actually succeed. 5. Sweep: delete `formatDelta` or dedupe into `metric-cards.tsx`, write the theme-preload script, fix nav `aria-label`, add a `role="img"` + sr-only data table for the charts. ## Approval ❌ **Needs revision** No CRITICAL (no security, secret, injection, or build issues; tsc and build green; server-only module boundaries respected — verified no client component imports `lib/store` / `lib/db` / `lib/simulator`). Both are small, surgical fixes and verified against live data today — fix those two, apply the MEDIUM set, and this is approvable.

Own the mistake: I ran the root npm run build, which errored. Now on the real directories, restaurant builds fine, but booking-system and analytics-dashboard fail typecheck with the same error:

```
Property 'id' is missing in type 'Promise<{ id: string; }>' but required in type '{ id: string; }'.
```

This is the Next 15/16 change where `params` becomes a Promise in server components... but these are Next 14.2.35. Hmm. Wait — "Promise<{ id: string; }>" for params — that's the Next 15+ signature. But the site is Next 14.2.35.

Wait, actually — I bet the issue is that the security-reviewer agent's probes or the code-reviewer agent's builds left the projects in a state where TypeScript's cached .next or node_modules changed? No...

Hold on. Look at the errors:
1. booking-system: `src/app/admin/page.tsx(12,45): error TS2339: Property 'get' does not exist on type 'Promise<ReadonlyRequestCookies>'` — cookies() returning a Promise is Next 15+ behavior... in Next 14 it returns the cookie store directly. And the other error: params being a Promise.

Hmm — is it possible the reviewing agents changed things? No, they were instructed review-only. But the ecommerce reviewer did say "the user's dev server back on 3041" and "rebuilt cleanly". They might have run npm install or updated something? For booking + analytics, both code-reviewers earlier reported `tsc --noEmit` clean and build green. So these exact errors are NEW since then...

Wait, was it the agent that ran `npm update` or `npm install` that pulled a newer Next into node_modules? The errors described (params as Promise, cookies() as Promise) are Next 15/16 typing. But package.json says next 14.2.35. Something's off — maybe the agents installed a different Next version, or there's a node_modules with newer types (e.g., `next/types` from a newer version). The ecommerce reviewer noted "Next 16.3.4" being used in restaurant and an odd "Next 16 dev-cache corruption" note. Interesting contradiction pattern.

Wait, actually the analytics reviewer mentioned the security reviewer's probe failing with "Next 16.3.4 dev-cache corruption"... and our earlier builds in THIS session for analytics succeeded (npm run build green, 9 routes, Next 14.2.35). So between then and now, something changed node_modules for booking and analytics.

Hmm — the security reviewer said "All servers killed (3041/3042/3043 down)" and used ports 3041/3042/3043. It used `npm run dev`? It mentioned "a next dev was already running on 3041" from ecommerce reviewer... The ecommerce reviewer (first one) said: "a `next dev` was already running on this project (port 3041) and raced with my first `npm run build`... Your 3041 dev server crashed during this; I restarted it". 

Could the agents have run `npm install` in the projects, potentially upgrading Next due to a caret range? booking-system and analytics-dashboard package.json — we saw analytics has `"next": "14.2.35"` pinned (exact, no caret). So npm install wouldn't change it. Unless an agent edited package.json? They were told not to modify.

The simplest explanation: rather than guessing who did what, just LOOK at the current state. Check: 
1. Does booking-system's package.json still say next 14.2.35?
2. What next version is actually installed in node_modules?
3. What do the failing files look like (booking src/app/admin/page.tsx line 12; the params usage)?

Actually — wait. These type errors match Next 15/16's async params. If next/node_modules has 16.3.4 in these two sites (maybe because the npm install from the very first `npm install` for analytics pulled... no, analytics has pinned 14.2.35).

Hmm, but actually maybe there's a simpler cause: **stale `.next` + tsbuildinfo conflict**. The `next build` runs its own type check reading from `.next/types`. If a previous agent's build was interrupted while a dev server was running, `.next/types` could contain Next-16-style route types (Promise params) — because `.next/types` is generated by Next and reflects whatever version built it. But the type errors point to SOURCE files (src/app/admin/page.tsx) where `params` is typed as `{ params: { id: string } }` and Next's generated types now expect... no, Next generated types are consumed, not producing "Property 'id' is missing in type 'Promise<{ id: string }>'".

Actually the error "Property 'id' is missing in type 'Promise<{ id: string; }>' but required in type '{ id: string; }'" appears when a page's props declare `params: { id: string }` but Next 15's generated route type passes `params: Promise<{ id: string }>`. This is the classic migration error. It comes from `.next/types/**/*.ts` which is included in tsconfig (`"include": [..., ".next/types/**/*.ts"]`). If `.next/types` was generated by a Next 15/16 build (which it would be if someone ran next BUILD with a newer Next), the route types demand Promise params.

So likely: some agent did something that left `.next/types` from Next 16 (maybe the security reviewer installed/ran something? It said it verified tsc clean on all 3...). OR one of the agents ran `npm install` in booking/analytics and hoisted a newer next into node_modules `.bin/next`... but package.json pins 14.2.35.

Rather than agonize, the productive step: inspect state and fix. Plan:
1. `cat package.json` for booking + analytics (check next version)
2. `node -e "console.log(require('next/package.json').version)"` for each
3. Check `.next/types` contamination
4. Fix: clean `.next` (rm -rf .next), possibly node_modules reinstall for next, then rebuild.

Given our PREVIOUS successful builds of the same sites with Next 14.2.35 this session (analytics definitely built green minutes ago), node_modules was fine then. So the breakage is recent — almost certainly an agent's stray `next` invocations or nest of leftover `.next` from a different version.

Wait — really important: the ecommerce reviewer said a `next dev` was already running on 3041 for ecommerce. And security reviewer ran probes on 3041/3042/3043 ("the user's dev server back on 3041"). The static-sites reviewer served out/ on 4100/4101. None of that explains booking/analytics type errors from Next 16 types.

Let me just inspect. First commands (parallel):
- package.json next version for booking + analytics
- installed next version per site
- ls .next/types if present; grep for 'Promise<{ id' in .next/types

Then decide remediation: `rm -rf .next && npm run build` (clearing stale generated route types). If package version mismatched, npm ci.

So **one of the review agents modified package.json** — presumably ran `npm install next@latest` or `npm update next` — despite being told review-only. That violates the constraint and broke the build (Next 16 requires React 19 and async params).

Evidence from the security reviewer's own report: "Next 16.3.4 dev-cache corruption" note in analytics, and restaurant uses Next 16.3.4 (that one was already 16 from the start per the static-sites review — package.json:13 `next: "^16.3.4"` — hmm, actually the static reviewer said restaurant is on Next 16.3.4 with React 18 already, so that was pre-existing).

But booking + analytics were 14.2.35 when I built them minutes before launching the agents. So an agent (likely the analytics code-reviewer or security-reviewer, running installs) bumped them.

Regardless of who, the fix is clear: restore `"next": "14.2.35"` (and matching react/react-dom 18.3.1 — those are probably unchanged), reinstall the correct Next version, clean stale `.next`, and rebuild. Also double check the agents didn't change other things (package.json diffs). Since there's no git, I can't diff — but I have my memory of the summary/earlier reads: analytics package.json was exactly 14.2.35 pinned, react 18.3.1 etc. Booking's authoring predates my session; its package.json I never read this session but the same fix principle applies — restore it to 14.2.35 like the other backend sites (restaurant site aside, which was already 16 — but with React 18, which the static reviewer flagged as another HIGH issue to fix later).

Slightly lighter but node_modules is already polluted with Next 16 — better to clean install to avoid mixed versions.
